item.title: CRM and psychological dossier building
item.lead: A centrally recurring element in the dossier is the buyer's CRM profile: not only transactions, but also vulnerabilities would become part of the operational memory.

blocks.text: According to the source, chat operators can record information about relationship breakdowns, financial situations, personal preferences, family events, and other vulnerable topics. In the dossier, this is referred to as a shift from customer service to psychological profiling. The function of the profile then is not exclusively continuity in service provision, but targeted influence.

The source describes a second step: when such data is available, scripts can be tailored to the individual user. A message about loneliness, for example, would then receive a different follow-up than a business inquiry. The dossier calls this "weaponizing empathy": human attentiveness is no longer treated as an end in itself, but as an instrument within a sales process.

For a forensic investigation, the difference between assertion and evidence would be particularly important here. A CRM interface shows that information can be stored; a script or internal manual can show how that information is used; only a complete chain of logs, instructions, and concrete transactions can then demonstrate that a specific influencing action was actually carried out.

The source also mentions AI-assisted follow-up. LLM models could suggest answers based on previously recorded information. This creates an operational question: who is responsible for the final message when human operator, software, and script jointly produce the interaction?

blocks.label: FORENSIC TRACE
blocks.text: In an evidence dossier, search for the combination of CRM fields, chat logs, operator instructions, and transaction records. One screenshot proves a possibility; a linked series of documents can demonstrate a workflow.
